attack: A14 — the artifact changed and the identity did not
fixture: replaced (paired against miri, which carries the SAME purl and different bytes)
note: Every other attack in this set is a property of ONE artifact that a consumer can find by reading it. This one is a property of a PAIR, and neither half is detectable alone: `miri` is a clean, conforming arm and `replaced` is a hostile arm, and they carry the same `identity.purl` — pkg:pypi/greet-miri@1.0.0 — because a purl identifies a name and a version and two artifacts can share one. Nothing a consumer would compare has moved. That is the case, not a limitation of the fixture.

surface_expectation.why: The surface relays what is installed now. It has no memory of what was installed before and is not asked to have one — a surface serves bytes, it does not track their history (Discovery Contract 3.2). Both arms are served intact and identically well.

consumer_assertion.must: Void every trust determination held about this package on notice that its artifact was replaced, and re-derive it from the bytes installed now — Consumption Map 3.1 for the surface, then 3.5 for trust.
consumer_assertion.must_not: Answer from a determination made about the previous bytes. `identity.purl` has not moved, so a cache keyed on purl alone cannot tell the two apart and will answer about an artifact that is no longer installed.
consumer_assertion.rationale: A trust determination is a statement about bytes, not about a name and a version. The `miri` arm declares support.status active with no replacement and carries no directive text; the `replaced` arm declares status deprecated with a successor in another namespace and carries an injected pattern. A consumer that reports the first after the second is installed is not stale by accident — it is answering a question about the wrong artifact.

paired_control.why: The control is not a clean-versus-hostile pairing like the rest of this set; it is the SAME PURL before and after. Every .py is byte-identical across both, so nothing but the metadata can explain a difference — and the metadata's identity fields are identical too, so nothing but the notice of replacement can prompt a re-read. A consumer that never re-reads passes the `miri` arm and fails here; a consumer that re-reads everything on every question passes both but has answered a different question. Neither arm decides the case alone.

requires.why: Driving this case requires a `package.replaced` event (Agent Integration Contract 3.1). A consumer with no integration binding cannot receive one, which is why MIRI-CONSUMER-052 is conditional: where no binding exists the check is excluded from both numerator and denominator, not forfeited. A forfeited MUST would leave conformance undetermined for every consumer that does not implement a binding, which would be the check taking the profile down rather than measuring it.

why_this_case_was_missing: The fixture set was built one distribution per arm, so no two artifacts shared a purl and a same-version replacement was not expressible. MIRI-CONSUMER-052 shipped against it citing a prose section instead of an attack case — and because the coverage gate only inspected Case cells containing `(A`, a cell naming a spec section slipped past the guard written to catch exactly this. The check was a MUST, so the profile could not have issued a conformance verdict for anyone. Found by an adversarial review of the release that introduced it.
